# DE-FAKE: Detection and Attribution of Fake Images Generated by Text-to-Image Generation Models
- **id:** defake-ccs2023
- **Authors / venue / year:** Zeyang Sha, Zheng Li, Ning Yu, Yang Zhang / ACM CCS 2023 (from memory; fetched arXiv page lists only cs.CR v2, Jan 2023) **[unverified]** / 2023
- **Links:** arXiv 2210.06998 · no code link in paper (authors 'will share')
- **Family:** attribution
- **Status:** partially-verified

## Summary (plain language)
Early study of detecting and attributing images from text-to-image diffusion models. Adding the CLIP embedding of the prompt to the image embedding improves 4-way source attribution (real / SD / LD / GLIDE). Also a common baseline in later attribution benchmarks.

## How it works
Image-only: ResNet18. Hybrid: CLIP image + CLIP text embedding concatenated -> 2-layer MLP; BLIP generates a prompt when none exists. Attribution = 4-class classifier. Unseen-model handling via a 0.9 confidence threshold (DALL-E 2).

## Training data
MSCOCO and Flickr30k prompts/real images; generators Stable Diffusion, Latent Diffusion, GLIDE, DALL-E 2 (DALLE2-pytorch). DALL-E 2 has only 1,028 (MSCOCO) and 300 (Flickr30k) fakes.

## Reported results
- Closed-set attribution accuracy (Table 2, MSCOCO / Flickr30k): image-only 0.864 / 0.863; hybrid natural prompts 0.936 / 0.933; hybrid BLIP prompts 0.903 / 0.892. (Introduction quotes different figures: 0.815 / 0.880 / 0.850; discrepancy not resolved.)
- Unseen-model adaptation (DALL-E 2) with 0.9 threshold: best of thresholds tried; numbers not extracted.
- Perturbations (JPEG/resize/blur): not evaluated. Fixed-FPR on real photos: not reported.
- Independent re-evaluation in WILD (wild-ijcnn2025, Table I): DE-FAKE balanced accuracy 94.00% plain -> 78.00% after 3 post-processing steps.

## Known weaknesses / failure modes
- Accuracy depends on prompt text (caption semantics) -> hybrid gain may reflect content/prompt alignment rather than generator traces.
- Cannot separate multiple unseen models (authors).
- Image-only detector weak on GLIDE and DALL-E 2 (authors).

## Relevance to this project
- Semantic (CLIP) features attribute well, but because the generators differ in how they render content, this is a content confound risk.
- No laundering robustness: do not rely on its numbers for in-the-wild attribution.
